researchQuestion: What is the correct authoritative identity model for a logical Emerald execution, and where should Emerald prevent contradictory terminal evidence from becoming accepted without destroying legitimate historical evidence?

scenarios.title: Two Valid Terminal Bundles (Same runId)
scenarios.setup: Two distinct exports of the same completed runId with differing export timestamps (bundleId1 != bundleId2)
scenarios.bundleA: runId: run-p39, status: COMPLETED, bundleId: b1
scenarios.bundleB: runId: run-p39, status: COMPLETED, bundleId: b2
scenarios.expected: Under pure content addressing, both bundles are accepted without cross-bundle runId uniqueness
scenarios.observed: Both accepted into archive/accepted/ as separate bundleId files
scenarios.securityImpact: Archive stores multiple valid certificates for the same logical run

scenarios.title: Contradictory Terminal Outcomes (COMPLETED vs FAILED)
scenarios.setup: One bundle claims COMPLETED, second bundle claims FAILED for the same runId; both have valid 2-of-3 threshold
scenarios.bundleA: runId: run-p39, status: COMPLETED, bundleId: b_comp
scenarios.bundleB: runId: run-p39, status: FAILED, bundleId: b_fail
scenarios.expected: Under pure content addressing, both contradictory bundles are accepted
scenarios.observed: Both accepted into archive/accepted/; external verifier receives contradictory authoritative outcomes
scenarios.securityImpact: CRITICAL: Content addressing alone fails to prevent contradictory terminal evidence

scenarios.title: Newer Checkpoint Followed by Older Checkpoint
scenarios.setup: Newer checkpoint 2 bundle ingested first, followed by older checkpoint 1 bundle
scenarios.expected: Content archive accepts both; no temporal or monotonic ordering enforced across bundles
scenarios.observed: Both accepted into archive/accepted/ in reverse temporal order
scenarios.securityImpact: Older evidence can be archived after newer evidence without ordering validation

scenarios.title: Terminal Bundle Followed by Non-Terminal Bundle
scenarios.setup: Final terminal COMPLETED bundle ingested first, followed by an intermediate RUNNING snapshot
scenarios.bundleA: runId: run-p39, status: COMPLETED, bundleId: b_term
scenarios.bundleB: runId: run-p39, status: RUNNING, bundleId: b_nonterm
scenarios.expected: Content archive accepts both; non-terminal evidence accepted post-termination
scenarios.securityImpact: Terminal state does not seal the run against subsequent intermediate snapshots

scenarios.title: Non-Terminal Bundle Followed by Terminal Bundle
scenarios.setup: Intermediate RUNNING snapshot ingested first, followed by final terminal COMPLETED bundle
scenarios.bundleA: runId: run-p39, status: RUNNING, bundleId: b_nonterm
scenarios.bundleB: runId: run-p39, status: COMPLETED, bundleId: b_term
scenarios.expected: Both accepted; legitimate intermediate monitoring succeeds
scenarios.securityImpact: Shows that legitimate intermediate snapshots must not be blocked by runId indexing

scenarios.title: Duplicate Terminal Export
scenarios.observed: First ingestion ACCEPTED; second ingestion returned DUPLICATE

scenarios.title: Crash Recovery Duplicate Terminal Exports
scenarios.setup: Pre-recovery and post-recovery terminal bundles exported with different supervisor lease evidence
scenarios.securityImpact: Crash recovery generates distinct valid bundleIds for the same runId

scenarios.title: Two Supervisors Produce Terminal Evidence
scenarios.setup: Two independent supervisors endorse distinct exports for the same runId
scenarios.securityImpact: Multi-supervisor authority requires logical execution coordination

scenarios.title: Worker Retries After Terminal State in Store
scenarios.setup: Worker attempts to execute actions or transition an already terminal run in SQLite
scenarios.expected: Coordinator and SQLite transaction throw; state machine rejects post-terminal mutations
scenarios.observed: Threw error; SQLite strictly enforces terminal finality locally
scenarios.securityImpact: Local SQLite state machine correctly fences terminal transitions

scenarios.title: Stale Worker Submits Evidence After Recovery
scenarios.setup: Stale worker submits evidence signed only by itself after supervisor recovery
scenarios.securityImpact: Threshold authority prevents stale uncoordinated worker evidence

scenarios.title: Valid Threshold Signatures on Stale Evidence
scenarios.setup: Worker and Supervisor sign an older intermediate snapshot
scenarios.expected: Accepted by content archive because content and signatures are valid
scenarios.securityImpact: Threshold signing does not enforce fresh state over stale snapshots

scenarios.title: Threshold Signatures on Conflicting Terminal Outcomes
scenarios.setup: Two bundles with conflicting terminal states (COMPLETED vs FAILED), each signed by 2-of-3 quorum
scenarios.expected: Both accepted; threshold signing operates purely over byte payloads, not cross-bundle run logic
scenarios.securityImpact: Threshold quorum alone does not resolve logical outcome conflicts

scenarios.title: Mismatched Contract Content Hash
scenarios.setup: Bundle claiming runId has contract contentHash mutated

scenarios.title: Mismatched Mission Contract Version
scenarios.setup: Bundle claiming runId has contract version mutated to 999

scenarios.title: Tampered Provenance Root
scenarios.setup: Bundle has provenanceRoot mutated without modifying payload
scenarios.securityImpact: Merkle provenance root integrity strictly verified

scenarios.title: Verification Evidence Omission / Failure in Terminal Bundle
scenarios.setup: Bundle claims COMPLETED but attempt exitCode is 1; fourfold derivation yields FAILED
scenarios.expected: Replay verifier derives FAILED; gateway quarantines with REPLAY_VERIFICATION_FAILURE
scenarios.securityImpact: Fourfold replay verification prevents unearned completion claims

candidateArchitectures.name: Strict runId Uniqueness in Archive
candidateArchitectures.rationale: Rejects all secondary bundles for a runId. Destroys multi-checkpoint auditing because intermediate checkpoint 1 blocks final terminal checkpoint 2.

candidateArchitectures.name: runId + Terminal Outcome Uniqueness
candidateArchitectures.rationale: Permits multiple non-terminal snapshots, but enforces at most one terminal certificate per runId. Fails if a crash-recovered terminal run produces a second terminal certificate.

candidateArchitectures.name: Monotonic Terminal Sequence
candidateArchitectures.rationale: Introduces terminalSequence counter. Unnecessary complexity since Emerald run lifecycles terminate at most once in SQLite.

candidateArchitectures.name: Authoritative Terminal Record Index
candidateArchitectures.rationale: Preserves pure content-addressing for evidence bytes in archive/accepted/{bundleId}.json, while introducing a separate logical execution index (runId -> AuthoritativeTerminalRecord) at the archival boundary. Completely resolves contradictory terminal evidence without breaking intermediate snapshots.

candidateArchitectures.name: Producer Terminal Export Fencing
candidateArchitectures.rationale: Fences export at the producing SQLite store. Does not protect remote/untrusted ingestion gateways from receiving contradictory synthetic bundles produced offline.

candidateArchitectures.name: Checkpoint-Bound Evidence
candidateArchitectures.rationale: Indexes by (runId, checkpointVersion). Solves intermediate checkpoint collision, but does not prevent contradictory terminal bundles sharing the same final checkpointVersion.

demonstratedGaps: Content-addressed evidence archiving indexes strictly on bundleId, allowing contradictory terminal outcomes (COMPLETED and FAILED) for the exact same runId to be accepted simultaneously into archive/accepted/.
Threshold Ed25519 signatures bind to payload bytes, but do not provide cross-bundle logical execution conflict detection.
demonstratedProperties: runId represents a single logical task lifecycle that strictly terminates locally in SQLite.
bundleId represents the exact immutable bytes of an evidence snapshot.
Multiple intermediate evidence snapshots per run are legitimate and essential for long-running mission auditing.
Option D (Authoritative Terminal Record Index) cleanly separates content identity from logical execution identity.
